subject: Cascade-10B: entry exception request + EU canary routing and fallback plan
summary: Request to allow a temporary onboarding exception for Cascade-10B in EU for a staggered canary. Calls out tokenizer mismatch and quantization drift; asks infra and product for routing/fallback policy and telemetry requirements.
messages:
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: maya@cascade.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Cascade-10B entry exception and EU canary routing

Team —

Cascade.ai shared the attached evaluation and asked to onboard their Cascade-10B variant into our EU catalog for a short staged canary. Quick context: their tokenizer differs from our usual base (some pre-tokenization leading to off-by-one tokenization in rare edge cases) and their recommended quantization profile produces ~6% delta on perplexity vs. our internal baselines. They’re requesting a 2-week entry window so they can run regen tests with customers in eu-west.

Asking for:
- A temporary version lock/exception so we can route EU production requests to cascade-10b-202611 until 2026-12-13 (2 weeks).
- Canary routing policy: start at 1% traffic, escalate to 5% then 25% if telemetry looks good.
- Fallback: automatic fallback to cascade-8b-v2 on any latency/regression or if model returns >1% rate of tokenization mismatch errors.
- Telemetry: please confirm which signals we’ll need for gating (latency p95, tokenization error rate, hallucination proxy metric, cost delta).

Attachments: cascade10b-eval-report.pdf (external eval), tokenizer-diff.txt (diff vs. our tokenizer), canary-rollout-plan.xlsx (proposed %s and timing).

Maya from Cascade is looped for acceptance criteria.

Can infra/product confirm feasibility and a short list of required telemetry dashboards + any concerns about autoscaling or batching with this variant?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior PM, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Cascade-10B entry exception and EU canary routing

Thanks Laura — this is OK in principle but need a couple specifics to scope infra work:

1) Canary traffic windows (dates + timezones).
2) Expected throughput (rps) at 1/5/25% to validate capacity planning.
3) Any nonstandard memory/kv-cache settings required by the model (I noticed Cascade recommends a high window for KV prefetch).

If you can fill those in I’ll patch the canary routing config and spin up a staging pool. I’ll also add a temporary variant tag so we can fall back at the routing layer.

- Dev

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, maya@cascade.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Cascade-10B entry exception and EU canary routing

Looping in technical notes from the runtime side — I ran a short staging run against cascade-10b-202611 and saw two items to call out:

1) Tokenizer mismatch: there are edge cases where the Cascade tokenizer collapses certain punctuation sequences differently than our standard tokenizer, which can cause off-by-one tokenization. That leads to KV cache indexing mismatch in long-chat scenarios (rare but observable in our 1k+ token synthetic tests). Attached tokenizer-diff.txt shows examples.

2) Quantization profile: their suggested 4-bit profile reduces memory but increases per-token generation variance; when combined with continuous batching at high concurrency we saw p99 latency spikes (likely due to kernel-switch thrash). We can mitigate by pinning the model to a dedicated CPU/GPU pool and restricting batching size for the canary.

Recommendations:
- Allow the temporary entry exception but with the following constraints:
  * Dedicated EU canary pool (no noisy neighbor burst scaling for first week).
  * Batching cap of 8 requests/step for user-facing endpoints during canary.
  * Telemetry gating: latency p95 < 350ms, p99 < 800ms, tokenization_mismatch_rate < 0.5%, hallucination_proxy (regression rate on eval prompts) < 1.5%.
  * Auto-fallback rule at routing layer to cascade-8b-v2 if any gating condition is breached for a 10-minute rolling window.

I’ll need the expected rps and canary windows from Product to size the dedicated pool. Also flagging that this variant will need a tokenizer-rule override in the tokenization service for the EU pool to avoid KV cache indexing issues — this is a small config but needs explicit approval.

-Karthik
Staff Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Cascade-10B entry exception and EU canary routing

Thanks — updated plan below with the numbers you asked for and explicit acceptance criteria. Please confirm you can enact the routing/config changes and the tokenizer override for the EU pool. If we agree, I’ll file the INF ticket and mark the calendar for the freeze window.

Planned canary window (EU local times):
- Start: 2026-12-01 18:00 UTC (1% traffic)
- Day 3: 2026-12-03 18:00 UTC (escalate to 5%)
- Day 7: 2026-12-07 18:00 UTC (escalate to 25%)
- End/freeze review: 2026-12-13 18:00 UTC (remove exception or extend based on results)

Traffic sizing (expected production baseline = 20k rps EU across all models):
- 1%: 200 rps
- 5%: 1,000 rps
- 25%: 5,000 rps

Runtime constraints:
- Dedicated EU canary pool sized for 6k rps sustained with headroom (Dev: please size to 7k to be safe).
- Batching cap 8 for user-facing endpoints; internal batch cache allowed for regen tests.
- Tokenizer override enabled for the EU pool (Karthik: see tokenizer-diff.txt attached).

Gating metrics (breach triggers immediate rollback):
- latency_p95 >= 350ms OR latency_p99 >= 800ms
- tokenization_mismatch_rate >= 0.5%
- hallucination_proxy >= 1.5%
- sustained error rate >= 1%

Rollback behavior: automatic routing to cascade-8b-v2 for any 10-minute rolling breach; on rollback infra will notify product and CS and pause further escalations.

Operational asks:
- Dev: create the temporary variant tag and route rule; confirm pool size and ETA to provision.
- Karthik: apply tokenizer override and confirm no KV cache index collisions for long chats in the EU pool.
- Priyom: please pull the evaluation prompt set into the canary telemetry dashboard so we can track hallucination_proxy and regression rate.

I'll create INF-4721 with the attachments and expected acceptance criteria, and Maya is good to run customer regen tests once the 1% canary goes live.

Thanks all — I appreciate quick confirmations so we can keep the window tight.

Laura Bennett
Senior PM, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference
